steps.title: The world
steps.subtitle: Discrete-event simulation, master seed 42
steps.headline: 1,847 cases through 24 activities
steps.narrative: A 7-day lifecycle is simulated from a seed-only random stream, so arrivals, case attributes and per-(case, stage) service shocks are identical in every run of this world. Case 1557 is the one this panel follows: it takes 22.32 h end to end against a population mean of 19.08 h, which puts it at the 75% mark.

steps.title: Process-time prediction
steps.subtitle: GradientBoostingRegressor, absolute-error loss
steps.headline: 77.7% better than mean
steps.narrative: M1 predicts how long each activity should take for this case from its attributes, the queue it arrived into and the hour of the week. What it cannot explain is the residual — and that residual is the signal M2 and M4 both read. The largest gap on case 1557 is Last mile: 15.73 h actual against 12.96 h predicted, 2.77 h unexplained.

steps.title: Bottleneck ranking
steps.subtitle: 0.45 queue-wait share + 0.30 utilisation + 0.25 unexplained residual
steps.headline: #1 Evidence review — 17.1% of total delay
steps.narrative: Every activity is scored on three things it can be guilty of: holding the queue, running hot, and taking longer than M1 can explain. Evidence review tops the ranking with 73.2% of the lifecycle's queue-wait, utilisation 0.84 and a wait-to-service ratio of 3.12 — cases spend 0.95 h waiting for 0.30 h of work.

steps.title: Anomaly detection
steps.subtitle: One IsolationForest per activity, fitted on healthy windows
steps.headline: 19 activities tripping
steps.narrative: Each activity has its own detector, fitted on the healthy baseline's weekday hours. A window counts only when it is both statistically unusual AND worse than the healthy 95th percentile on wait or utilisation, and a stage only trips after two sustained flags — contamination alone would flag 5% of perfectly healthy hours. Evidence review is flagged in 22% of its windows (43 hours), first sustained flag 8.00 h after the constraint started.

steps.title: Agent investigation
steps.subtitle: Select by impact x uncertainty, probe, hypothesise, drill or stop
steps.headline: Evidence review at p=1.00
steps.narrative: The agent does not walk the activity list. It scores every unprobed activity by impact times uncertainty, spends a probe on the highest, and re-scores. It used 2 of its 6 probes and stopped because evidence_review identified as capacity_saturation at p=1.00; the best remaining probe (document_verification) scores 0.060 against a floor of 0.069, so it would not change the answer — not because it ran out.

M4 attributes this to capacity_saturation (p=1.00).

nodes.label: Evidence review:weekday
nodes.reasoning: Selected weekday at evidence_review: the stage delay is more concentrated along this dimension than any other left (information 0.43), so it is the question that narrows the explanation most. evidence_review by weekday: Mon and Sun carry 87.1% of the queue wait on 36.2% of the volume (x2.4), mean wait 3.17 h. This narrows where the capacity_saturation at evidence_review bites.

steps.title: Delay-cause classification
steps.subtitle: Three classes: capacity saturation, staffing shortage, normal
steps.headline: Capacity saturation (p=1.00)
steps.narrative: M4 reads the strained hours at Evidence review and separates two failure modes that look identical in a KPI table. Staffing shortage is capacity below the activity's own normal roster for part of the week; capacity saturation is a roster that is constant and simply too small. The verdict is weighted by the delay in each window and taken at the peak of the queue, not across the hours spent draining it — draining always looks like saturation, because the full roster is flat out. Trained on its own synthetic fault corpus, never on this run.

steps.title: Intervention impact
steps.subtitle: Paired counterfactual re-simulation, seeds 42 / 43 / 44
steps.headline: 1.10 h off mean cycle, best case
steps.narrative: There are no past interventions to regress on, so M5 does not predict — it re-runs the world. Each candidate is simulated three times against three paired baselines that share an identical arrival stream and identical per-case service shocks, so the difference is the intervention and nothing else. That is why a 95% interval at n=3 is this narrow. Add 2 claims evidence reviewers moves mean cycle by 1.10 h (95% CI 0.07 h to 2.13 h).

steps.title: ROI optimisation
steps.subtitle: Greedy ROI-per-rupee under one shared budget
steps.headline: Pre-check claim evidence packets before reviewer queue, Add 2 claims evidence reviewers selected, ROI 0.76
steps.narrative: Benefit is hours saved times 270 cases a day over 30 days at Rs 12 an hour of holding cost, plus the SLA penalties avoided. An action only becomes eligible once that beats its own price — leftover budget is not a reason to buy something that loses money. Rs 165,000 of the Rs 250,000 cap is committed, returning Rs 290,159 over the horizon.

steps.title: Outcome
steps.subtitle: Re-simulated with the selected portfolio on the same seed
steps.headline: 0.93 h off mean cycle time
steps.narrative: The chosen action set is applied to the configuration and the whole world is simulated again on the same master seed, so the only difference is the intervention. Mean cycle falls from 19.08 h to 18.15 h and cost per case from Rs 238 to Rs 224. The constraint moves: Document verification is now the highest-ranked activity at 8.5% of total delay, which is the world the agent would re-plan against.
